title: Sleep Lab
tagline: Do I snore? Fitbit Air SpO2 meets overnight audio.
summary: A local pipeline that lines up my Fitbit Air's overnight blood oxygen and sleep stages with snore events picked out of a bedroom recording by YAMNet, then asks whether SpO2 dips follow the snoring. The full pipeline runs and is tested on synthetic nights; real nights are next. Along the way Fitbit's API turned into the Google Health API, four days before the old one switches off.
highlights: Built against the new Google Health API (v4) rather than the Fitbit Web API, which reportedly stops working on 30 Oct 2026
Privacy by construction: audio is scored in one-minute chunks and thrown away, keeping only snore timestamps and a few 4-second clips
Every 'SpO2 dips after snoring' claim is tested against shuffled random onsets, so wrist-sensor noise can't pass as a finding
Next: three real nights, then Garmin runs via MCP and a snore detector fine-tuned on my own clips
